name: Delta Air Lines
blurb: Major U.S. carrier with a large narrowbody and widebody fleet. Configurations vary by registration and retrofit status.

glance.cabins: Delta One business on long haul widebodies, Delta Premium Select premium economy, Delta First on domestic flights, Delta Comfort extra legroom rows (formerly Comfort+), and Delta Main economy
glance.seatTip: Delta Comfort rows sit at the front of economy, so check which rows the map marks before you settle for a regular Delta Main seat.

name: United Airlines
blurb: U.S. network carrier operating domestic and long haul fleets. Cabin layouts differ across subfleets.

glance.cabins: United Polaris business on long haul widebodies, United Premium Plus premium economy, Economy Plus extra legroom rows, and standard economy
glance.seatTip: Economy Plus rows sit at the front of economy, so check which rows the map shades before paying for an upgrade.

name: American Airlines
blurb: U.S. carrier with extensive A321 and 737 fleets. Seat maps below are schematic reconstructions of typical public layouts.

glance.cabins: Flagship Business on long haul widebodies, Flagship Suite seats with privacy doors on the newest premium configured aircraft, Premium Economy on select long distance flights, First on domestic narrowbodies, Main Cabin Extra extra legroom rows, and Main Cabin
glance.seatTip: Main Cabin Extra rows sit near the front of economy and at some exit rows, so check which rows the map shades before paying for more legroom.

name: British Airways
blurb: UK flag carrier. Short haul A320 family and long haul widebody configs vary by aircraft and route.

glance.cabins: First on selected long haul aircraft, Club Suite business class with a door on most long haul aircraft, World Traveller Plus premium economy, World Traveller economy, and Club Europe and Euro Traveller on short haul flights
glance.seatTip: Older long haul aircraft can still carry an earlier business cabin, so check the seat map on your booking rather than the route alone.

name: easyJet
blurb: European low cost carrier operating an all Airbus A320 family fleet with largely single cabin layouts.

glance.cabins: One economy cabin on an all Airbus fleet, with paid Up Front and Extra Legroom seat options
glance.seatTip: Extra Legroom seats are in the first row and the overwing exit rows, and exit rows come with safety rules on who can sit there.

name: Southwest Airlines
blurb: U.S. low cost carrier with an all Boeing 737 fleet and primarily single cabin layouts. Configurations vary by subfleet.

glance.cabins: An all Boeing 737 fleet with assigned seating, including Extra Legroom seats near the front and at the exit rows, and standard economy seats
glance.seatTip: Southwest moved from open seating to assigned seats, so choose your seat when you book or check in rather than relying on boarding position.

name: JetBlue
blurb: U.S. carrier known for A320 family aircraft and select Mint premium cabins. Layouts differ by route and retrofit.

glance.cabins: Mint business class with lie flat seats on longer flights, the new BlueFirst domestic first class from 8 December 2026, EvenMore extra legroom seats, and Main economy
glance.seatTip: BlueFirst is being installed aircraft by aircraft and may appear only on some dates, so check the seat map on your booking rather than the route alone.

name: Alaska Airlines
blurb: U.S. carrier operating mainly Boeing 737s. First, Premium, and Main cabin products vary across the fleet.

glance.cabins: First Class, Premium Class extra legroom economy, and Main Cabin on the Boeing 737 fleet, with regional jets on shorter routes
glance.seatTip: Premium Class rows sit just behind First and add legroom without the First fare, which makes them a good value pick on longer domestic flights.

name: Lufthansa
blurb: German network carrier with short haul A320 family and long haul widebody fleets. Cabin products differ by aircraft.

glance.cabins: New Allegris long haul cabins on selected Airbus A350 and Boeing 787 aircraft, older First, Business and Premium Economy cabins on other widebodies, and Business and Economy on European flights
glance.seatTip: Allegris is only fitted to part of the fleet, so the same route can have very different seats from one day to the next. Check the aircraft on your booking.

name: Air France
blurb: French flag carrier operating short haul narrowbodies and long haul widebodies. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

glance.cabins: La Premiere on selected Boeing 777 aircraft, Business on long haul widebodies, Premium on most long haul aircraft, Economy, and Business and Economy on European flights
glance.seatTip: Air France has been refitting its long haul fleet in stages, so two flights on the same route can have different business seats. Check the aircraft on your booking before you pick.

name: Ryanair
blurb: European ultra low cost carrier with a high density Boeing 737 fleet. Single cabin layouts are typical.

glance.cabins: One economy cabin on a Boeing 737 fleet, with paid Premium seats offering extra legroom at the front and over the wings
glance.seatTip: Seats are assigned at random unless you pay, so if sitting together matters, choose seats when you book.

name: Emirates
blurb: Dubai based long haul carrier operating large widebody fleets. Multi cabin products vary substantially by aircraft and retrofit.

glance.cabins: First class on the Airbus A380 and Boeing 777, Business class, Premium Economy on newer and refitted aircraft, and Economy
glance.seatTip: Emirates flies more than one layout of the same aircraft type, so confirm the configuration shown on your booking before you pick a seat.

name: Qatar Airways
blurb: Doha based network carrier with modern widebody fleets. Business and economy layouts differ by subfleet.

glance.cabins: Qsuite business class with closing doors on many Boeing 777 and Airbus A350 aircraft, First on the Airbus A380, standard business class on other aircraft, and Economy
glance.seatTip: Qsuite is not on every aircraft, so check the seat map for your exact flight before you book a premium seat.

name: Turkish Airlines
blurb: Istanbul based network carrier with a large narrowbody and widebody fleet. Cabin products and densities vary by aircraft and route.

glance.cabins: Business Class with lie flat seats on widebody aircraft, Business Class on narrowbody flights, and Economy Class
glance.seatTip: Long transfers at Istanbul are common, so on overnight legs a window seat away from the galley is worth choosing early.

name: Air Canada
blurb: Canadian network carrier with narrowbody domestic fleets and long haul widebodies. Cabin products and densities vary by aircraft and retrofit.

glance.cabins: Air Canada Signature Class with lie flat suites on Boeing 777, Boeing 787, Airbus A330 and Airbus A321XLR aircraft, North America Business Class, Premium Economy on widebodies, and Economy with Preferred seats
glance.seatTip: Air Canada Rouge and Air Canada Express flights use different cabins from mainline aircraft, so check who operates your flight before you choose a seat.

name: Singapore Airlines
blurb: Singapore based long haul carrier known for premium heavy widebody fleets. Layouts differ substantially by aircraft and cabin product generation.

glance.cabins: Suites on the Airbus A380, First on some Boeing 777s, Business class, Premium Economy, and Economy
glance.seatTip: Singapore Airlines runs several cabin versions on its long haul fleet, so check the seat map for your exact flight rather than the aircraft type alone.

name: Cathay Pacific
blurb: Hong Kong network carrier operating A350, 777, and A330 fleets. Business and economy layouts vary by subfleet.

glance.cabins: Aria Suite business on retrofitted Boeing 777 aircraft, business on the Airbus A350, plus premium economy and economy on long haul widebodies
glance.seatTip: The same aircraft type can carry an older or newer business cabin, so check the configuration your flight shows.

name: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines
blurb: Dutch flag carrier with short haul narrowbodies and long haul 787/777/A330 fleets. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

glance.cabins: World Business Class with lie flat seats on long haul aircraft, Premium Comfort premium economy, Economy Comfort extra legroom seats, Economy, and Europe Business on short haul flights
glance.seatTip: KLM Cityhopper regional jets have different cabins from mainline Boeing and Airbus aircraft, so check who operates your flight.

name: Virgin Atlantic
blurb: UK long haul carrier operating A350 and 787 fleets. Premium and economy products differ by aircraft.

glance.cabins: Upper Class with a fully flat bed and direct aisle access, Retreat Suites on selected Airbus A330neo aircraft, Premium, and Economy including Economy Delight seats with extra legroom
glance.seatTip: Economy Delight is an Economy fare with up to 34 inches of pitch, not the separate Premium cabin, so check which one you are booking before you compare seats.

name: Iberia
blurb: Spanish network carrier with short haul A320 family and long haul A330/A350 fleets. Cabin layouts vary by registration.

glance.cabins: Business, Premium Economy and Economy on long haul Airbus A330 and A350 aircraft, and Business and Economy on short haul A320 family flights
glance.seatTip: On short haul flights Business uses standard seats with the middle seat kept free, so the gain is space and service rather than a bigger seat.

name: Qantas
blurb: Australian flag carrier with domestic 737 fleets and long haul widebodies. Cabin products and densities vary by aircraft and route.

glance.cabins: First on the Airbus A380, business, premium economy, and economy on long haul widebodies, and business plus economy on domestic Boeing 737 flights
glance.seatTip: Domestic and long haul layouts are very different, so match the aircraft on your booking to the right map below.

name: Etihad Airways
blurb: Abu Dhabi based long haul carrier operating A380, 787, and narrowbody fleets. Multi cabin layouts differ by subfleet and retrofit.

glance.cabins: The Residence and First Apartments on the Airbus A380, Business Studios and Economy on most widebodies, and Business and Economy on narrowbody flights
glance.seatTip: Cabin products vary by aircraft type, so confirm whether your flight is an A380, a Boeing 787 or a narrowbody before comparing seats.

name: Hawaiian Airlines
blurb: Hawaii based carrier with A321neo interisland/US mainland hops and long haul A330/787 widebodies. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

glance.alliance: No alliance (part of Alaska Air Group)
glance.cabins: First and Main Cabin with Extra Comfort rows on mainland and interisland flights, plus premium cabins on long haul widebodies
glance.seatTip: On flights from the mainland, a window on the side facing the islands is a favourite on approach, but check the aircraft type first because layouts differ.

name: Spirit Airlines
blurb: U.S. ultra low cost carrier with a high density A320 family fleet. Single cabin layouts and paid seat selection are typical.

glance.cabins: Big Front Seat rows at the front and standard Economy seats behind on an Airbus A320 family fleet
glance.seatTip: Seat selection is usually an extra fee on low fares, so compare the price of a Big Front Seat with a standard seat before you pay for either.

name: SWISS
blurb: Swiss flag carrier (Lufthansa Group) with short haul A320 family and long haul A330/777 fleets. Cabin products vary by aircraft.

glance.cabins: First on long haul Boeing 777 and selected widebodies, Business on all long haul aircraft, Premium Economy on most long haul aircraft, Economy, and Business and Economy on European flights
glance.seatTip: Long haul business uses a staggered layout, and some rows have single seats with extra surface space on both sides. Solo travellers often pick those first.

name: ANA (All Nippon Airways)
blurb: Japanese network carrier with domestic narrowbodies and long haul 787/777 fleets. Business and economy layouts differ by subfleet.

glance.cabins: THE Suite first and THE Room business on selected Boeing 777 aircraft, plus business, premium economy, and economy on other long haul widebodies
glance.seatTip: Long haul business products differ by aircraft, so confirm the aircraft type on your booking before comparing seats.

name: Japan Airlines
blurb: Japanese network carrier with domestic narrowbodies and long haul 787/777/A350 fleets. Cabin products and densities vary by aircraft and retrofit.

glance.cabins: First, Business, Premium Economy and Economy on long haul widebodies, with Class J and Economy on many domestic flights
glance.seatTip: Cabins differ by aircraft and retrofit, so check the aircraft type on your booking before you pick a row on a long haul flight.

name: Korean Air
blurb: South Korean flag carrier operating narrowbody regional fleets and long haul 777/787 widebodies. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

glance.cabins: Prestige Class business and Economy across the fleet, with First on some long haul aircraft
glance.seatTip: Layouts vary between the Airbus and Boeing widebodies, so confirm the aircraft on your flight before choosing between window and aisle pairs.

name: Air New Zealand
blurb: New Zealand flag carrier with Pacific narrowbody flying and long haul 787/777 fleets. Layouts differ by subfleet and route.

glance.cabins: Business Premier, Premium Economy and Economy on long haul Boeing 787 and 777 aircraft, with Economy Skycouch rows that convert into a flat space
glance.seatTip: Economy Skycouch rows are sold as a set of seats in a row, so they suit couples or a parent with a child on long overnight flights.

name: Norwegian
blurb: Norwegian low cost carrier focused on narrowbody 737 and A320 family flying. Single cabin high density layouts are typical.

glance.cabins: A single Economy cabin on a Boeing 737 fleet, with extra legroom seats sold at exit rows and near the front
glance.seatTip: Exit row seats give the most legroom on a single cabin 737, but they come with age and mobility rules and often a fee.

name: Scandinavian Airlines (SAS)
blurb: Scandinavian network carrier with short haul A320 family and 737 fleets plus select long haul types. Cabin products vary by aircraft and route.

glance.cabins: SAS Business, SAS Plus and SAS Go on long haul Airbus widebodies, with SAS Plus and SAS Go in Europe
glance.seatTip: SAS Plus on European flights usually sits in the rows at the front, so it suits travellers who want a quick exit after landing.

name: Frontier Airlines
blurb: U.S. ultra low cost carrier with a high density A320 family fleet. Single cabin layouts and paid seat selection are typical.

glance.cabins: Economy on an Airbus A320 family fleet, with paid upgrade seats near the front and at exit rows
glance.seatTip: Seat selection is usually an extra fee on basic fares, so decide whether legroom or a quick exit matters most before paying for a seat.

name: Wizz Air
blurb: Hungarian ultra low cost carrier with an all Airbus A320 family fleet. High density single cabin layouts and paid seat selection are typical.

glance.alliance: Not a member of an airline alliance
hubs: Budapest (home base), with many more bases across Central and Eastern Europe
glance.cabins: A single economy cabin with high density seating; seat selection is normally a paid extra
glance.seatTip: Without a paid seat you are assigned one at check in, so pick a seat early if sitting together or by an exit matters.

name: Aer Lingus
blurb: Irish flag carrier (IAG) with short haul A320 family flying and transatlantic A321LR/A330 services. Cabin products and densities vary by aircraft and route.

glance.cabins: Business and Economy on transatlantic Airbus A330 and A321 long range aircraft, and Economy with extra legroom options on European routes
glance.seatTip: Many flights to the United States from Dublin and Shannon offer US preclearance, so allow time at the airport rather than relying on a seat near the door.

name: Finnair
blurb: Finnish flag carrier hubbed at Helsinki with A320 family short haul and A350 long haul fleets. Business is often dynamically sized on narrowbodies.

glance.cabins: Business, Premium Economy and Economy on long haul Airbus widebodies, with Economy and a European business offer on narrowbodies
glance.seatTip: Helsinki connections are often short, so a seat near the front of Economy can help you leave the aircraft sooner on a tight transfer.

name: WestJet
blurb: Canadian carrier with a large Boeing 737 fleet plus Boeing 787-9 long haul aircraft. Premium and all economy subfleets coexist after network changes.

glance.cabins: Business, Premium and Economy, with lie flat Business on Boeing 787 Dreamliners
glance.seatTip: WestJet flies both Boeing 737 and 787 aircraft, so check the aircraft type on your booking before choosing a row.

name: Austrian Airlines
blurb: Austrian flag carrier (Lufthansa Group) with short haul A320 family flying and long haul 787/777 fleets. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

glance.cabins: Business, Premium Economy and Economy on long haul Boeing widebodies, and Economy with a European business offer on narrowbodies
glance.seatTip: On European flights business usually uses regular seats with the middle seat kept free, so compare the fare against an extra legroom row before upgrading.

name: EVA Air
blurb: Taiwanese network carrier known for Royal Laurel business and strong premium economy products on 777/787 fleets, plus A321 narrowbodies for regional flying.

name: TAP Air Portugal
blurb: Portuguese flag carrier hubbed at Lisbon with A320 family European flying and A330neo long haul routes. Cabin products and densities vary by subfleet and route.

name: LATAM Airlines
blurb: LATAM Group network carrier spanning South America with A320 family narrow bodies plus 787 and 777 long haul aircraft. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

name: Air India
blurb: Indian flag carrier with a growing A320neo domestic and regional fleet plus 787 and 777 long haul aircraft. Cabin products are changing through fleet renewal.

name: Thai Airways
blurb: Thai flag carrier hubbed at Bangkok with A350 and 787 long haul fleets plus select 777 aircraft. Premium and economy products vary by aircraft and route.

glance.cabins: Royal First on some Boeing 777 aircraft, Royal Silk business class, Premium Economy on some of the longest routes, and Economy
glance.seatTip: Cabins differ sharply by aircraft type on THAI, so match the aircraft on your booking to a card below before you pick a seat.

name: LOT Polish Airlines
blurb: Polish flag carrier hubbed at Warsaw with 737 narrow bodies, Embraer regionals, and 787 long haul aircraft. Layouts differ by subfleet and route.

name: Aeromexico
blurb: Mexican flag carrier hubbed at Mexico City with a large 737 fleet plus 787 long haul aircraft. Premium and economy products vary by aircraft and route.

name: Ethiopian Airlines
blurb: African Star Alliance carrier hubbed at Addis Ababa with a large 787 and A350 long haul fleet plus regional narrow bodies. Cabin products and densities vary by subfleet and route.

name: Malaysia Airlines
blurb: Malaysian flag carrier hubbed at Kuala Lumpur with A330 and A350 long haul flying plus 737 narrow bodies for regional routes. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

name: IndiGo
blurb: Indian low cost carrier with a large A320 family fleet and ATR turboprops for thinner routes. Most flying is dense single class economy with select extra space rows.

name: Copa Airlines
blurb: Panamanian Star Alliance carrier hubbed at Panama City with an all Boeing 737 narrow body fleet linking North and South America. Premium and economy products vary by aircraft.

name: Avianca
blurb: Colombian Star Alliance carrier with A320 family narrow bodies and 787 long haul aircraft. Cabin products and layouts differ by subfleet and route.

name: Saudia
blurb: Saudi flag carrier hubbed at Jeddah and Riyadh with 777 and 787 long haul fleets plus A320 family narrow bodies. Premium and economy products vary by aircraft and route.

name: Vietnam Airlines
blurb: Vietnamese SkyTeam flag carrier hubbed at Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City with A321 narrow bodies plus 787 and A350 long haul aircraft. Cabin products and densities vary by subfleet and route.

name: Philippine Airlines
blurb: Philippine flag carrier hubbed at Manila with A321 family narrow bodies plus A330, A350, and 777 long haul flying. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

name: Garuda Indonesia
blurb: Indonesian SkyTeam flag carrier hubbed at Jakarta with 737 narrow bodies and A330 plus 777 long haul aircraft. Cabin products and layouts differ by subfleet and route.

name: Aegean Airlines
blurb: Greek Star Alliance carrier hubbed at Athens with an A320 family fleet for European and regional flying. Premium and economy products vary by aircraft and route length.

name: Vueling
blurb: Spanish low cost carrier in the IAG group with a large A320 family fleet based around Barcelona and other Spanish hubs. Most flying is dense single class economy with select extra space rows.

glance.alliance: Not in a global alliance (part of the IAG group)
glance.cabins: Single cabin Economy on an Airbus A320 family fleet, with paid Space One (row 1), Space Plus (rows 2 to 4) and Space (exit row) seats
glance.seatTip: Space seats in the exit rows give the most legroom for the price, but they have no underseat storage, so plan to put your bag in the overhead locker.

name: EgyptAir
blurb: Egyptian Star Alliance flag carrier hubbed at Cairo with 787 and 777 long haul fleets plus A320 family narrow bodies. Premium and economy products vary by aircraft and route.
